graph.name: Appway: Securing Sensitive Banking Workflows with Isolated Architecture on AWS
graph.notes:
Provide web applications for financial services institutions, which have tough security requirements.
    use of cloud organizations and aws accounts for isolation of resources, e.g, each customer has its own account.
    Whenever possible, use DevOps tools like TerraForm or Puppet to manage the whole infrastructure as code.
    There are other services not shown in the graph, e.g., AWS Single Sign-On, CloudWatch, CloudTrail, Key Management Service.

nodes.name: Cognito
nodes.notes: NOTES: flexibility: can start with simple; provide advanced features like MFA; later can transit to a more sophisticated setup (e.g., with Okta, Microsoft Active Directory)

nodes.name: EFS
nodes.notes: NOTES: connect all EC2 instances within the cluster

nodes.name: EC2
nodes.notes:
SCALERANGE: 3+ appway cluster nodes in different AZs
WORKLOAD_PEEK: The core Appway is a Java-based web application on a Apache Tomcat server. Front-end is built with React (HTML, JavaScript, CSS); the backend is all Java with Jersey as REST framework. Internally use Hazelcast to connect multiple Appway instances to one Appway cluster.

nodes.name: S3
nodes.notes: DATA_PEEK: a serverless management tool; React-based single-page application

nodes.name: Lambda
nodes.notes: WORKLOAD_PEEK: Execute management tasks, e.g., setup new AWS account, provision new Appway cluster

nodes.name: ControlTower
nodes.notes: NOTES: enforces policies for every account created by AWS Organizations, e.g., encryption on EBS volumes
